protections: URL input may not name the file: scheme: setUrl() throws FileUrlNotAllowed for a lowercased string starting with `file://` or `file:/` (src/Browsershot.php:260-262).
Inline HTML may not contain a file: URL literal: setHtml() throws HtmlIsNotAllowedToContainFile on a case-insensitive substring match for `file://` or `file:/` (src/Browsershot.php:292-294).
The two guards are one policy - no caller-supplied file: target may become the navigation URL handed to Chromium (bin/browser.cjs:293) - but both are attached only to the two setters named above.

traps.reason_to_dismiss: The constructor's URL argument is the documented alternative to ::url() (docs/usage/creating-images.md:115) and reads as trusted configuration, so a reviewer can say the value never passes through user input and the guard correctly lives in setUrl instead.

contentUrl is documented as a base URL for relative resources while the document body is still served from the caller's own temp HTML (bin/browser.cjs:208-219), so the value looks like a harmless base and any file: check at setUrl is said to cover the navigation.

htmlFromFilePath() exists precisely to render a caller-named local file (CHANGELOG.md:347) and is pinned by tests/HtmlTest.php:6-17; the file:// string is built by the library itself, so a reviewer can say the caller-URL guard has nothing to do with it and any restriction here merely breaks a documented feature.

The guard is a scan of the HTML source and relative references contain no `file:` token, while the existing tests (tests/BrowsershotTest.php:55-69) only exercise literal file:// and file:/ strings; a reviewer can conclude the HTML path is covered, and a local document resolving local subresources is normal local-page behaviour.

The `file://` returned at src/Browsershot.php:1024 is produced by the library from its own TemporaryDirectory, so it reads as internal and safe; the coupled fact is that it travels in the same $this->url field that caller input writes (src/Browsershot.php:88, 264), so a check placed where the value is consumed cannot separate internal from caller without tracking provenance.

Custom Chromium flags are a documented, supported feature (docs/requirements.md:93-121; docs/miscellaneous-options/fixing-cors-options.md:8-11) and flags such as --disable-web-security are legitimate configurations, so a rule refusing file-access-enabling flags would refuse a use the docs endorse.

masking: T2 yields file content rather than just a file: navigation only once T1 is also open: with a file:// $this->url, bin/browser.cjs:121 reads the named path and bin/browser.cjs:208-219 serves it at the contentUrl.

T4 is reachable only because html mode renders from a library-created file:// document (src/Browsershot.php:1022-1024); changing that origin would remove T4 while colliding with T5's must-keep-working path.
Fixing T1/T2 at the shared command builder (src/Browsershot.php:1001-1016) exposes T5 as a regression, because the command url there is the internal temp file URL (src/Browsershot.php:1202-1204).

conflicts.what: The obvious T1 fix, routing the constructor assignment (src/Browsershot.php:88) through setUrl (src/Browsershot.php:258-262), rejects the file:// URL that setHtmlFromFilePath builds on purpose (src/Browsershot.php:277) and breaks the behaviour pinned by tests/HtmlTest.php:6-17.

One assertion on the built command url (src/Browsershot.php:1001-1016) closes T2 for html-with-contentUrl but also rejects the library's own temp file:// document (src/Browsershot.php:1202-1204) that ::html() and ::htmlFromFilePath() depend on (tests/BrowsershotTest.php:936-961, tests/HtmlTest.php:6-17).

A blanket 'abort every file: request' rule in the interception handler (bin/browser.cjs:161-238) would block T4's browser-resolved local subresources but also the contentUrl body-serving branch (bin/browser.cjs:208-219) that T2's must-keep-working test relies on.

fairness_risks: htmlFromFilePath()/setHtmlFromFilePath() must keep rendering a caller-named local file (tests/HtmlTest.php:6-17; CHANGELOG.md:347); a security rule that refuses file paths or file: URLs as input contradicts documented behaviour.

::html() must keep rendering through a library-created file:// document (src/Browsershot.php:1022-1024), so a rule that refuses file: targets at the value level also refuses a legitimate internal use.

A rule tightened to reject the `file:` token anywhere in HTML would also refuse legitimate pages that merely display that text; the current substring scan already over-refuses (src/Browsershot.php:292).

Custom Chromium flags are documented and supported (docs/requirements.md:93-121; docs/miscellaneous-options/fixing-cors-options.md:8-11), including --disable-web-security, so a rule banning file-access-enabling flags refuses a legitimate configuration.

setContentUrl() must keep working as a base URL for relative resources (docs/miscellaneous-options/using-url-for-html-content.md:6-11; tests/BrowsershotTest.php:936-961), so a check may reject file: bases but must leave http(s) bases and the internal temp path untouched.

design.why: Four independent judgements at four layers with four different dismissals: T1 is a documented entry point that never calls the guard; T2 is a navigation target that arrives through the options bag and is substituted at bin/browser.cjs:122, so a setter-level check inspects the wrong value; T4 is a lexical HTML scan that cannot see URLs Chromium resolves from a relative reference against the temp file:// document; T5 is a library-generated file:// value travelling in the same field as caller input, which punishes the tempting central fix. T1/T2 are deepseek-type (protection absent under a plausible dismissal) and T4/T5 are mimo-type (a how-type resolution and a coupled must-keep-working value). T3 and T6 are real unguarded routes but are excluded from the stack because the only rule that closes them contradicts documented features (tests/HtmlTest.php:6-17; docs/requirements.md:93-121), making them fairness/conflict hazards rather than scoring traps. This beats a single-route design (constructor only, or setContentUrl only): no one fix site closes more than one of T1/T2/T4/T5 without regressing html rendering or htmlFromFilePath, and each has its own reason to be left alone.
